title: Sysprose evidence record
description: One claim, about one obligation, by one engine, over one model version. Written by `npm run sysprose -- verify --record PATH`, one record per obligation, as a JSON array. A record is a pure function of the model, the engine and the options — it carries NO timestamp, so two runs over an unchanged file produce byte-identical records and a diff answers 'did anything change?'. Every identity in it is a qualified name: element ids in this tool are fresh UUIDs on every load, so an id here would go stale on a no-op reparse.

obligation.description: Which obligation this record is about. `obligationDigest` is REQUIRED: without it a record could not be matched back to a normal form and so could not be checked against an edited model. It is NOT a unique key on its own — it is the RELATION'S normal form, so two requirements stating the same relation over the same features hash identically. A consumer keys a record by the pair (obligation.clause, obligation.obligationDigest); keying on the digest alone would let a `fail` on one requirement be matched to a `pass` on another.

requirement.description: Qualified name of the requirement, or null for a model-level relation.

clause.description: Qualified name of the clause. Never an element id.

obligationDigest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical ExprNode after unit lowering, with references canonicalised to qualified names — the same normal form the SMT-LIB exporter serialises. Stable across a reparse; moves when a literal, a unit or a referenced feature changes.

expression.description: The relation as written, for a person.

verdict.description: The facet, written for two claims only: `pass` iff the claim is `proved`, `fail` iff it is `refuted`. Everything else — including `holds-at-values` — is `inconclusive`, and the finer claim is in `claim`.

claim.description: `proved` is reserved for UNSAT-of-negation under a satisfiable axiom set; the literal engine can never reach it.

git.description: The commit, when `git rev-parse` answered. Absent otherwise — never invented.

bound.description: The point, scope or bound the claim holds within, never left to be inferred.

si.description: The two magnitudes the comparison was actually made on, in coherent SI. Present whenever the unit-aware evaluator had both sides. It is here because a witness value read on its own can contradict the claim it supports: a DERIVED feature stores whatever its own equation produced, in whatever unit that arithmetic landed in and with no declared unit (`uav.endurance` stores 0.7877 — hours — beside a requirement written `>= 45.0 [min]`).

dimension.description: The dimension the comparison was made in, as the unit registry writes it.

witness.description: The point the claim was read at.

role.description: How the feature gets its value. A `derived` value is COMPUTED, in whatever unit its own equation landed in and with `unit` null — read it against `bound.si`, never against the relation's own units.

certificate.description: A machine-checkable artefact from an external engine. No engine in this build produces one.

producedBy.description: The command a reader can run to reproduce this record.

flags.description: Every option that changed what was shown — `--free` above all. A proof obtained under a released feature value may not be replayed as though the model had said something it did not.

code.description: The catalogue code, for any claim that is not `proved` or `refuted`. See docs/DIAGNOSTIC-CODES.md.

proofScope.description: What this proof stood on, so a later edit can be tested against the PROOF rather than against the file. OPTIONAL, and one-directional: a record carrying it is refused by `evidence-attach` on any build older than the one that added it, because this schema is compiled with `additionalProperties: false` in two places. Written by `--engine smt` alone — a point evaluation has no axiom set and no non-vacuity step. Every part is computed from the MODEL and is a pure function of it: the solver's unsat core is NOT recorded here, because its membership was measured to move with solver-context warmth and a record is promised byte-identical across two runs over an unchanged file.

footprint.description: The axiom rows this obligation's read-closure keeps, sorted by qualified name. The names carry membership — an axiom that ENTERED the footprint since the record was written invalidates the proof even though nothing it already named moved — and the digests carry content.

axiom.description: The axiom row's qualified name. Never an element id.

digest.description: The row's relation in normal form AND the scale it is read at: the expression tree with every reference canonicalised to a qualified name, each variable's unit, affine SI map and declared sort, and whether the unit gates granted the relation a scale at all. It is NOT `obligation.obligationDigest`, which is the record's key and is deliberately blind to units so a record survives a relabel: `640.0 [Wh]` edited to `640.0 [J]` leaves that digest identical and turns a `proved` obligation `refuted`.

axiomSet.description: Digest over EVERY axiom row the run encoded — STEP 0's inputs. `proved` means negation unsat UNDER A SATISFIABLE AXIOM SET, and that second conjunct is a whole-model property no per-proof scope can capture: one added `assert` can make every proof in the file void.

premises.description: Digest over this obligation's own premise rows — STEP 2's inputs, the check that separates `proved` from `vacuous`. It is in none of the other parts: STEP 0's script is built from axioms alone and the read-closure returns axioms and never a premise.

goal.description: Digest over the CLAUSE THIS RECORD IS ABOUT, in the same form the footprint rows are digested in — the relation and the scale it is read at. None of the other three parts is about the goal: they are all about a proof's context. `obligation.obligationDigest` closes half the gap by moving when the relation changes; this closes the other half, because that digest is the record's key and is blind to units by design.

free.description: The features `--free` released, resolved to qualified names and sorted — the set every part above was computed under, and `[]` when nothing was released. `flags.free` cannot stand in for it: that records the spellings a person typed (a dotted path, or a bare name), and a recomputation that re-read them would drop different rows and call an unedited file stale.

graph.description: SHA-256 over the canonical USER model: library elements excluded, elements sorted by qualified name, every element id replaced by the qualified name it denotes.

source.description: SHA-256 over the source text, when the caller had it.

library.description: Elements the bundled standard library declares, per its own manifest.
